items.title: LLM 基盤と kagent v0 を全部 k8s に入れてみた / Deploy both LLM and kagent v0 in k8s
Hand over intent as specs (Requirements, a done condition, and tests that check them) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 03
items.summary: Level 300. This deck shows how to hand your intent to Kiro as a spec: expand a one-sentence request into requirements with EARS acceptance criteria, decide what done looks like before the work starts, and write down what must not change. On a small booking app, it then connects the spec to checks, with property-based tests that find a counterexample and mutation testing that shows weak tests as a number. This is deck 03 (Guide pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.

items.title: Observability and evals (Traces, metrics, and the Evals SDK) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 09
items.summary: A deck for Python developers who have built an Agent with Strands Agents and now want to see what it does and check how well it answers. It shows how to read the metrics in the AgentResult, send OpenTelemetry spans with StrandsTelemetry to the console, a file, or an OTLP endpoint, add your own span attributes, and turn on the SDK logs. It then runs a first evaluation with the Strands Evals SDK (Cases, an @eval_task task, OutputEvaluator, and Experiment), explains evaluator levels and TracedHandler, compares tool order with TrajectoryEvaluator, diagnoses a failed run with diagnose_session, and adds red teaming, a simulated customer, chaos testing, evaluation of production traces, and strands-evals in CI. Most examples were run on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region and are shown with their real output (strands-agents 1.64.0, strands-agents-evals 1.9.0). The deck says which ones were not run: the OTLP and Jaeger setup, and the CloudWatch trace provider. The facts come only from the official Strands Agents documentation, and the examples use a help-desk agent for a made-up online shop with made-up customers and orders, built for this series. This is deck 09 (Verify) of the Learn Strands Agents with Kiro series, Level 300, as of November 2026.

items.title: Structured output and streaming (Typed answers and streamed answers) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 06
items.summary: This Level 200 deck shows how to get typed values from a Strands Agents agent with a Pydantic schema (structured_output_model, the validation retry, the forced retry and the attempt limit) and how it works, using the official docs and real output from Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region. It also covers streaming answers with stream_async and callback handlers, returning them from FastAPI, and the order and contents of the events, as deck 06 (Go deeper) of the series Learn Strands Agents with Kiro.

items.title: Rules and context (Steering, Skills, Powers, and code intelligence) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 02
items.summary: Level 200. Context is a limited resource, so this deck shows where to put the rules for Kiro: steering that is always read, steering read with matching files, and skills and powers opened only when needed. It also shows what to write (what Kiro missed and what the code can't tell it) and, on a small booking app, how to check whether the rules worked. This is deck 02 (Guide pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.

items.title: Make it remember (Short-term and long-term memory in AgentCore Memory) | Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro 03
items.summary: This Level 300 deck shows how to make a help desk agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime remember its customers with AgentCore Memory. With no memory, an agent meets every customer as new. Figures with the official AWS icons explain short-term memory (the events of one inquiry), long-term memory (the preferences and facts kept across inquiries), how namespaces keep them apart per customer (actorId), and the 4 built-in strategies that make long-term records. With real terminal lines from an English copy of the help desk from deck 01, it adds a user preference strategy, shows the record made from the preference a customer gave in inquiry 1, and shows the help desk using that preference in another inquiry without asking again. It also covers the measured time until a record exists (about 62 seconds on this help desk), keeping customers apart, how long memory is kept, keeping injected instructions out of memory, memory and RAG, the pricing units, and the record that stayed after a strategy was removed. Deck 03 (Build it out) of the series Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro.

items.title: Strands harness | Kiro と学ぶ Strands Agents 10
items.summary: Strands harness (strands-harness) の create_harness() で組み立て済みの Agent を作り、道具と指示を足して絞り、session と memory で会話と知識を残し、interventions と sandbox で止めどころを決めて本番に出すまでを、strands-harness 0.3.4 で動かしたコードと出力で説明します。Python は書けて Strands Agents は初めての開発者向けの Level 200 の資料です。

items.title: Device Modeling Report: SPICE Model for LTspice – AK60-39 V3.0 KV80
items.summary: This document is a device modeling report by Bee Technologies Inc. detailing the SPICE model (for LTspice) for the CubeMars AK60-39 V3.0 KV80 robotic actuator (PMSM + 39:1 planetary gearbox). The report covers the equivalent circuit model, extracted model parameters, and comparison results between SPICE simulations (verified with ngspice-42) and manufacturer specifications or digitized characteristic graph data at 48 VDC. Key updates in Revision 1.1 include fitting speed and DC input current curves, integrating an equivalent FOC driver circuit (FOC_DRV), and implementing saturable inductance and flux linkage.
